messages.subject: NA of activity-relevant values of the last three days in the All Important Variable.output.csv
parts:
Dear Dr. van Hees,

 

I wrote this letter to you due to the problems encountered when using GGIR.

 

The subjects tested for 14 days (12/6 13:30 - 12/20 13:00), and the activity-relevant values of the last three days showed NA.I guess this was due to not enough effective hours (valid day).

I try to turn off the following functions.

 

Save_ms5raw_without_invalid= FALSE, (I thought this function was opened to delete the data that have no valid hours),

But it has no effect and the result was still the same.

The relevant values of the activity in the next three days showed NA (as shown in the attached figure)

 

Would you be able to tell me how to change the settings so that I can see the activity value for these three days?

 

Further, I have read the previous response in this group.

"The default GGIR settings should be reasonable for most purposes. The part 2 analysis will by default require at least 16 hours of valid data per day (midnight-midnight) while the sleep analysis require the same number of valid hours for thewindow defined from noon-noon. In part 5 the day time inclusion criteria is by default 2/3 of the waking hours."

I wonder the definition of 'the waking hours', whether which means noon to noon or not ? is the maxumun 24 hours? if so, i had thought the waking should be less than 24 hours (cut the sleep period?)

 

Attached the file with R setting, code, and results

Sincerely 

Look forward to your response~

Sam

The subjects tested for 14 days (12/6 13:30 - 12/20 13:00), and the activity-relevant values of the last three days showed NA.I guess this was due to not enough effective hours (valid day).
Where exactly do you see the NA values? Inside one of the csv reports? If yes, which one? I am looking at the pdf, but I am not sure what you are referring to.

I try to turn off the following functions.

Save_ms5raw_without_invalid= FALSE, (I thought this function was opened to delete the data that have no valid hours),
​What do you mean by "turn off", do you mean that it was set to save_ms5raw_without_invalid = TRUE and now you have set it to Save_ms5raw_without_invalid = FALSE?
I wonder the definition of 'the waking hours', whether which means noon to noon or not ? is the maxumun 24 hours? if so, i had thought the waking should be less than 24 hours (cut the sleep period?)

Waking hours are only defined in part 5, and run from waking up to sleep onset.​ So, probably somewhere around 12 to 18 hours per day. In theory this window can be fairly long, but as it is always constrained between two SPT windows and in GGIR those SPT windows are expected to occur in a 48 hour window.
Attached the file with R setting, code, and results

​A milestone file (.RData extension) from the meta/basic folder would be help to reproduce the problem.

Thanks, Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] NA of activity-relevant values of the last three days in the All Important Variable.output.csv
parts: Dear Sam
1. As far as I know, sleep efficiency = SleepDurationInSpt / SptDuration;

The widely accepted calculation is time in bed divided by the total duration of sleep after sleep onset. This is why GGIR does not report sleep efficiency in part 4 output if you do not have a sleep diary that asks about time in bed and argument sleepwindowType = "SPT" (default). However, sometimes researchers use your equation,  for example when time in bed is not known. This is why I included it only in part 5 and not in the part 4 output. Maybe the documentation on this can be a bit clearer.
I wonder how SleepDurationInSpt is calculated? If I want to calculate SleepDurationInSpt can I find these elements in part4 or part5 table?

It is the sum of all sustained inactivity bouts that overlap with the guider, this cannot be derived from other variables in the csv report, but is derived inside GGIR. However, if you export the time series you would be able to verify the calculation.
Is this window guider_SptDuration used to define the period of time the subject is in bed, and if so, what is the meaning :(SleepDurationInSpt / guider_SptDuration )?

Hopefully my first answer above clarifies this.

Vincent
Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/
